trust_boundaries: Internet to Edge Layer (Browser to Nginx)
Edge Layer to App Layer (Nginx to Flask API)
App Layer to Data Layer (Flask API to PostgreSQL)
architecture_summary.operational_context: Cloud-hosted three-tier web application with public internet ingress via Nginx, Flask API in a private application subnet, and PostgreSQL in a private data subnet; no autonomous agent components.

threat_actors.name: External opportunistic attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Financial gain through data theft, credential abuse, or service disruption
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Internet-facing Nginx or Flask API vulnerabilities, credential stuffing, or brute force against the login endpoint
non_capabilities: No physical access to cloud infrastructure
No pre-existing insider knowledge or valid credentials
No direct access to private application or data subnets
Cannot modify cloud provider-managed hypervisor or network fabric

threat_actors.name: Malicious or compromised insider
threat_actors.motivation: Data exfiltration, sabotage, or misuse of legitimate access for personal or financial gain
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate credentials or deployment access to the Flask API or PostgreSQL environment
non_capabilities: No physical access to cloud hardware
No ability to bypass network segmentation without valid credentials
Limited to assigned role permissions and approved tooling

attack_paths.entry_point: Public internet to Nginx reverse proxy
attack_paths.impact: Initial foothold on the edge host; possible proxy bypass, request smuggling, or pivot toward the application layer
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Nginx is internet-exposed and a high-value target, but a patched baseline and minimal modules reduce exploitability.

attack_paths.entry_point: Internet login through Nginx to Flask API using stolen credentials
attack_paths.impact: Authenticated access to application data and API actions
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Credential stuffing and phishing are common against public login endpoints, and MFA is only partially enforced.

attack_paths.entry_point: Crafted HTTP request through Nginx to Flask API
attack_paths.impact: Remote code execution or SQL injection leading to confidential data access or modification
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: The Flask API accepts untrusted input and has direct database access, while secure coding and input validation are only partially implemented.

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised Flask host or misconfigured deployment artifact
attack_paths.impact: Disclosure of PostgreSQL credentials enabling direct database access
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Secrets management is planned but not fully implemented, and exploitation requires host compromise or deployment misconfiguration.

attack_paths.entry_point: Privileged access to the PostgreSQL host or data directory
attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of database files containing confidential data at rest
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires privileged host access or insider access to the data subnet, and encryption at rest is partially implemented.

attack_paths.entry_point: Adjacent network position in the application or data subnet
attack_paths.impact: Capture of database credentials and sensitive query data in transit
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Private subnets and partial TLS reduce sniffing opportunity, and the attacker must first obtain a network foothold.

attack_paths.entry_point: Public internet traffic flood against Nginx
attack_paths.impact: Service unavailability for the web application
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: The internet-facing endpoint is exposed to volumetric and application-layer DoS, and DDoS protection is only partially implemented.

attack_paths.impact: Account takeover and unauthorized access to application data
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: The login endpoint is internet-exposed, and account lockout and MFA are only partially enforced.

mitigations.control_name: Baseline configuration of IT systems is created and maintained
Users and assets are authenticated commensurate with risk
Establish and maintain a secure application development process
Identities and credentials are issued, managed, verified, revoked, and audited
Communications and control networks are protected

findings.severity_rationale: Internet-exposed Nginx with partial hardening could be exploited for initial access, but high attack complexity and minimal modules reduce likelihood.
Stolen valid credentials bypass network controls and grant authenticated API access, while MFA is only partially enforced.
The public Flask API accepts untrusted input and has direct database access, so an injection flaw could expose or alter confidential data.
Credentials stored in files on the Flask host would require host compromise but could yield direct database access.
Database files at rest contain confidential data, but exfiltration requires privileged host or data-subnet access.
Unencrypted database traffic could expose credentials and sensitive queries, but private subnets and partial TLS reduce exposure.
Internet-facing Nginx is exposed to volumetric and application-layer DoS, though partial DDoS controls reduce impact.
The exposed login endpoint permits credential brute force, but lockout and MFA partially mitigate account takeover.
